body.objective: Students will be able to read a short francophone text.
body.iCan: I can read a short francophone text.
successCriteria: I can read and understand a short francophone text
I can analyze characters, plot and themes in French
I can write a personal and critical response
body.hook: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's "Le Petit Prince" has been translated into more than 500 languages. It's a children's book about a tiny prince from an asteroid, and also a book adults read to understand love, loss and what really matters. Francophone literature often works on two levels at once.

study.title: Lire « Le Petit Prince »
study.question: How do I read and respond to francophone literature in French?
study.passage:
Contexte : « Le Petit Prince » (1943), d'Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, pilote et écrivain français. Le narrateur, un aviateur, tombe en panne dans le désert du Sahara. Il rencontre un petit garçon venu d'une autre planète.
Résumé du chapitre 21 (en français simple) : Le petit prince rencontre un renard. Le renard lui demande de l'« apprivoiser », c'est-à-dire de créer des liens. Chaque jour, le petit prince s'assoit un peu plus près. Ils deviennent amis. Quand le petit prince part, le renard est triste, mais il dit que c'est bien, car maintenant les champs de blé lui rappelleront les cheveux dorés du prince. Avant de partir, le renard lui donne un secret : « On ne voit bien qu'avec le cœur. L'essentiel est invisible pour les yeux. »
Analyse : Personnages (le petit prince, le renard), intrigue (rencontre, amitié, séparation), thèmes (l'amitié, la responsabilité, ce qui est vraiment important), symboles (le blé, la rose).
Film option: the 2015 animated film "Le Petit Prince" (Mark Osborne) or a francophone short film chosen by the teacher.
Task: Answer comprehension questions, then write a response: what the fox's secret means to you and an example from your life.
study.source: Summary written for this lesson; the short quotation is from Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, "Le Petit Prince" (1943).
steps: Learn about the author and context
Analyze characters, plot, themes and symbols
Write a personal and critical response
discussion: Pourquoi le blé est-il important pour le renard ?
Que signifie « l'essentiel est invisible pour les yeux » ?
Pourquoi les adultes lisent-ils aussi ce livre ?
study.product: Write a 200-word response in French: summarize the passage, explain one theme and one symbol, and connect the fox's secret to your own life.

examples.title: Vocabulary
examples.problem: What does "apprivoiser" mean in the story?
examples.answer: To tame, to build a bond

examples.title: Symbol
examples.problem: Why will the wheat fields matter to the fox?
examples.answer: They will remind him of the prince's golden hair
examples.explore: What does this say about friendship?

examples.title: Theme
examples.problem: State a theme of the chapter in French.
examples.answer: L'amitié demande du temps et crée des responsabilités

examples.title: Quote
examples.problem: Explain "L'essentiel est invisible pour les yeux."
examples.answer: What matters most, like love and friendship, can't be seen, only felt

practice.q: Where does the narrator crash his plane?
Which animal does the prince meet in chapter 21?
How do the prince and fox become friends?
practice.a: The prince sits a little closer each day.
One sees clearly only with the heart; what is essential is invisible to the eyes.

practice.q: Name a theme of the chapter.
What year was the book published?
Why do adults also read this book?
practice.a: It explores deep themes like love, loss and values beneath a simple story.

practice.q: Explain the symbol of the wheat.
practice.a: It becomes meaningful because it reminds the fox of his friend.

practice.q: How does the fox's secret apply to modern life?
practice.a: Answers vary, for example valuing people over appearances or possessions.

practice.q: Write a sentence in French explaining a theme.

misconceptions: Thinking children's books can't have deep themes
Translating word by word instead of using context
exitTicket: Name the two characters in chapter 21.
Explain the fox's secret in your own words.
